notes:
ATTEMPT 3. The MAJOR is resolved, and the cause of it is worth recording because it applies to a whole family of options.

Attempts 1 and 2 rendered this on a PLAIN WHITE shirt. Bias cutting is a GRAIN DIRECTION, and on plain cloth a grain direction is invisible — so the photograph showed literally nothing of the option being sold. The blueprint communicates the bias with diagonal HATCHING over the collar panel, and hatching on plain cloth photographs as nothing at all. The image was not slightly wrong; it was empty.

Rendering the shirt in a fine vertical navy stripe makes the grain of every panel directly legible, and the option becomes obvious in one second: the collar's stripes run diagonally while the body's run vertically, and the two meet at the collar seam. There is precedent as well as logic — shirt/canvas-normal, passed earlier today, was rendered striped and its bias angle was measurable to a tenth of a degree.

The general rule this establishes for the whole bias_cutting field, and for any future option whose subject is grain, weave or nap direction: THE CLOTH MUST CARRY A PATTERN THAT REVEALS DIRECTION. Choosing plain cloth for such an option is not a neutral styling decision — it deletes the subject.

All nine categories at or above 95 with zero Critical or Major findings, so this qualifies for the logged waiver at attempt 3.
